p: God is good to Israel: As it were between hope and despair he bursts forth into this affection, being assured that God would continue his favour toward such as were godly indeed, and not hypocrites.
no bands in their death: The wicked in this life live at pleasure and are not drawn to death like prisoners: that is, by sickness which is death's messenger.
Therefore pride compasseth them about as: They glory in their pride as some do in their chains, and in cruelty, as some do in apparel.
set their mouth against the heavens: They blaspheme God, and do not fear his power and rail upon men, because they esteem themselves above all others.

people return hither: Not only the reprobate, but also the people of God often fall back seeing the prosperous estate of the wicked, and are overwhelmed with sorrows, thinking that God does not correctly consider the estate of the godly.
say: Thus the flesh moves even the godly to dispute with God concerning their poor estate, and the prosperity of the wicked.
I will speak thus: If I give place to this wicked thought, I offend against your providence, seeing you do all things most wisely and preserve your children in their greatest dangers.
sanctuary of God: Until I entered into your school and learned by your word and Holy Spirit that you order all things most wisely and justly.
utterly consumed with terrors: By your fearful judgment.
thou awakest: When you open our eyes to consider your heavenly happiness, we contemn all their vain pomp.
beast before thee: For the more that man goes about by his own reason to seek out God's judgments, the more he declares himself a beast.
with thee: By faith I was assured that your providence always watched over me to preserve me.
heaven but thee: He sought neither help nor comfort of any save God only.
portion for ever: He teaches us to deny ourselves, to have God our whole sufficiency, and only contentment.
go a whoring from thee: That is, forsake you to seek others.
to draw near to God: Though all the world shrinks from God, yet he promises to trust in him and to magnify his works.
